info.name: RallyHub API
info.description:
RallyHub API (apps/api, NestJS). Generated from the controllers, DTOs, services and *.http.spec.ts suites on branch chore/api-dev-tooling.

## Setup
- Use the Postman desktop app (or the web app with the Desktop Agent) so the cookie jar works. Auth is cookie-based: Better Auth sets `better-auth.session_token` and Postman sends it back automatically. Cookies for the API host (e.g. `localhost`) must be allowed: in Postman open Cookies (under the Send button) and make sure the API domain is not blocked; if you use pm.cookies in scripts, add the domain to the allowlist there too.
- Pick an environment: **RallyHub Local** (API on http://localhost:3001, web origin http://localhost:3000) or **RallyHub Dev** (fill in the REPLACE_ME values). Set `userPassword` to a password of your choice (8+ chars); never commit a real one.
- Better Auth calls send `Origin: {{webOrigin}}`; the API must list that origin in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.
- Routes: Tenant, Tenant members, Court booking and Open play are URI-versioned (`/v1/...`). Health, Users, Venues and Courts are not versioned. There is no global prefix. Every route needs a session unless its description says Public.
- Context headers: `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` (tenant members, venue create) and `X-Venue-Id: {{venueId}}` (court list/create, booking). Unknown ids are ignored, which gives 400 "... context required".
- Rate limit: 100 requests per 60 s by default, then 429 for 60 s.
- If the API runs with AUTH_DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL set, every request is treated as that user and the cookie is irrelevant; leave it unset to test permissions.

## Suggested run order
1. Auth > Sign up (owner) (or Sign in (owner) if the user exists). Saves `userId`.
2. In a terminal at the repo root: `npm run dev:make-admin -w api -- dev-owner@example.com` (use your `ownerEmail`; add `--remote` when the API's DATABASE_URL is not on localhost, e.g. the shared dev DB; `--revoke` undoes it). Admin status is read from the database on each request, so no new sign-in is needed.
3. Users > Get current user (sanity check).
4. Tenant > Create tenant (saves `tenantId`), then Tenant > Update tenant status (ACTIVE).
5. Tenant members > Add member: adds you as tenant-wide OWNER. A platform admin can already manage everything else, but Open Play > Enable needs a real staff membership. (First-owner claim: a non-admin can add themselves as the first OWNER only when their email equals the tenant's email, is verified, and the tenant has no members yet; email/password sign-up is unverified, so locally the admin adds the first owner.)
6. Venues > Create venue (saves `venueId`, `venueSlug`), Venues > Update venue (status ACTIVE), Venues > Replace booking settings.
7. Courts > Create court (saves `courtId`).
8. Court booking > Create booking: a public Open Play game 3 days ahead at 18:00 Asia/Manila (saves `bookingId`, `openPlayJoinToken`, `bookingReferenceId`).
9. Open play > List public games, View game by join link, Manage view, Set visibility.
10. Auth > Sign up (second user) (this switches the session). Try the owner-only requests to see 403s: Tenant > Create tenant, Tenant > Update tenant details, Tenant members > List members, Venues > Update venue, Courts > Create court (with X-Venue-Id), Open play > Manage view. Then Open play > Join via public listing (201), Leave game (204), Cancel game (403, not the booker).
11. Auth > Sign in (owner), then Open play > Cancel game (204).
12. Cleanup / destructive last: Tenant members > Update / Remove member (409 on the last owner), Courts > Delete court and Venues > Delete venue (409 once bookings exist), Tenant > Delete tenant (soft, sets INACTIVE).

## Chaining variables (set by test scripts)
userId, secondUserId (sign up / sign in); tenantId (Create tenant); memberId (Add member); venueId, venueSlug (Create venue); courtId (Create court); bookingId, openPlayJoinToken, bookingReferenceId, bookingStart (Create booking). privateBookingId is manual (see Enable Open Play).

request.description:
**Who may call:** Public (`@AllowAnonymous()`).

**Success:** 200 `{ "status": "ok", "message": "Hello World!" }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 429 when the rate limit is hit (default 100 requests / 60 s per client, then a 60 s block).

**Notes:**
- Not versioned. When AUTH_DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL is set on the API, every request (this one included) is treated as that user.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Better Auth endpoints (basePath `/api/auth`). Every request sends `Origin: {{webOrigin}}`. The session cookie (`better-auth.session_token`) is stored by Postman's cookie jar for the API host and sent on every later request. Only one session is held at a time per host: signing in as another user replaces it.

header.description: Better Auth rejects auth calls whose Origin is not in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Public.

**Success:** 200 `{ token, user: { id, email, name, emailVerified: false, ... } }` and a session cookie (auto sign-in). Saves `userId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 422 when a user with that email already exists (use Sign in instead).
- 400 for an invalid email or a password shorter than 8 characters.
- 403 when Origin is missing/untrusted (check BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS on the API).

**Notes:**
- Email/password sign-up leaves `emailVerified` false (no verification is configured). Platform-admin status cannot be set here; extra fields such as `isPlatformAdmin` are ignored.
- Next: grant yourself platform admin with `npm run dev:make-admin -w api -- {{ownerEmail}}` (add `--remote` when DATABASE_URL points at a non-local host).

header.description: Better Auth rejects auth calls whose Origin is not in BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Public.

**Success:** 200 `{ redirect: false, token, user }` and a session cookie. Saves `userId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 for a wrong email or password.
- 403 when Origin is missing/untrusted.

**Notes:**
- Use this to switch back to the owner after testing as the second user.

**Notes:**
- Same endpoint as Sign up (owner). The second user is a plain signed-in user with no memberships: use it to see 403s and to join Open Play games.

item.name: Tenant
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/tenant/...`. A new tenant starts as PENDING; bookings need the tenant, venue and court all ACTIVE.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin only (`assertPlatformAdmin`).

**Success:** 201 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201). Saves `tenantId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 403 for everyone who is not a platform admin (tenant owners and staff included). Spoofed body fields like `actorId` / `isPlatformAdmin` are stripped.
- 400 when `email` is not an email or `tenantName` / `phone` are missing.

**Notes:**
- Required: `email`, `tenantName`, `phone`. Optional: `tenantOwnerName`, `primaryColor`.
- The tenant `email` matters for the first-owner claim rule (see Tenant members > Add member).

query.description: Optional. Only return the tenant if it has this status (PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE); otherwise 404. Not validated by a DTO.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Any signed-in user. The service performs no membership or admin check on this read.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 "We couldn't find that tenant." for an unknown id, or when `status` is given and does not match.

**Notes:**
- The route is declared as `find/:id/` (trailing slash); Express's default non-strict routing serves it with or without the slash.
- Unclear: `status` is read with a bare `@Query` and passed to Prisma unvalidated; a value outside the enum is likely to surface as a 500, not a 400. Not covered by tests.

**Who may call:** Platform admin only.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201) with the new status.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (checked before permissions, so any signed-in user sees 404 for a missing id).
- 403 for non-admins, owners included.
- 400 when `status` is not one of PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE.

**Notes:**
- Set ACTIVE before booking: bookings and Open Play joins need tenant, venue and court all ACTIVE.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant (`assertCanEditTenant`). STAFF cannot.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else, including staff, venue staff, inactive owners and owners of other tenants.
- 400 when `email` is not an email.

**Notes:**
- All fields optional (partial of Create tenant): `email`, `tenantName`, `phone`, `tenantOwnerName`, `primaryColor`.

**Who may call:** Platform admin only.

**Success:** 200 `{ success, message, statusCode, data: Tenant }` (note: the body's `statusCode` field is always 200 even when the HTTP status is 201); the tenant is not removed, its status becomes INACTIVE.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown tenant (before permissions).
- 403 for non-admins.
- 400 "This tenant is already inactive/deleted." when it is already INACTIVE.

**Notes:**
- Destructive for the rest of the run order: an INACTIVE tenant's courts are no longer bookable. Run last, or set the status back with Update tenant status.

item.name: Tenant members
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/tenant-member/...`. Every request needs tenant context: `X-Tenant-Id: {{tenantId}}` (an `X-Venue-Id` of a venue in the tenant also works). The tenant always comes from that header, never from the body. Missing or unknown tenant id → 400 "Tenant context required".

header.description: Resolves tenant context (looked up in the DB; an unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Tenant context required").

request.description:
**Who may call:** An active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant, or a platform admin. Otherwise only the first-owner claim: role OWNER, no `venueId`, `email` equal to the caller's own email AND to the tenant's email, the caller's email verified, and the tenant has no member rows at all (`isValidFirstOwnerClaim`).

**Success:** 201 `{ message, content: TenantMember }` where TenantMember is `{ id, userId, tenantId, venueId, role, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt }`. Message is "Member added successfully!..." for a new row, or "Member is reactivated" when an inactive row in the same scope was reactivated. Saves `memberId`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context, an invalid email, a role other than OWNER | STAFF, a non-UUID `venueId`, OWNER with a `venueId` (owners are always tenant-wide), or a `venueId` from another tenant.
- 403 for callers who are neither owner nor admin and do not meet the first-owner claim.
- 404 when no user has that email (the user must sign up first; email match is exact, and Better Auth stores emails lowercased).
- 409 when the user already has an active row in the same scope, or "Lots of changes are being made..." when the tenant lock is busy.

**Notes:**
- As sent, this adds the signed-in owner as tenant-wide OWNER. A platform admin can do everything else without a membership, but Open Play > Enable Open Play only accepts venue staff (OWNER/STAFF memberships), so run this before that request.
- The first-owner claim needs `emailVerified: true`, which email/password sign-up does not set, so in local testing a platform admin adds the first owner.
- To try Update/Remove member, change the body to `{ "email": "{{secondEmail}}", "role": "STAFF" }` (optionally `"venueId": "{{venueId}}"`) and send again; `memberId` then points at that row. Updating/removing the only owner gives 409.

request.description:
**Who may call:** An active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant, or a platform admin.

**Success:** 200 `{ message, content: TenantMember }` where TenantMember is `{ id, userId, tenantId, venueId, role, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context, OWNER with a `venueId`, or a venue outside the tenant.
- 403 for everyone else.
- 404 when the member id is not an active member of this tenant.
- 409 "A tenant must keep at least one active owner..." when this would demote the last active owner; 409 when the user already has a row in the target scope, or the tenant lock is busy.

**Notes:**
- Body fields are optional: `role` (OWNER | STAFF) and `venueId` (UUID, or `null` for tenant-wide). `email` is ignored.
- As sent (demote to venue STAFF) this returns 409 if `memberId` is the tenant's only owner; point it at a second member first (see Add member).

request.description:
**Who may call:** An active tenant-wide OWNER of this tenant, or a platform admin.

**Success:** 200 `{ message, content: TenantMember }` where TenantMember is `{ id, userId, tenantId, venueId, role, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt }` with `isActive: false` (soft delete; re-adding the same scope reactivates it).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context.
- 403 for everyone else.
- 404 when the member id is not an active member of this tenant.
- 409 when removing the last active owner, or the tenant lock is busy.

item.name: Venues
item.description: Not versioned: `/venues/...`. All routes need a session (none are public). Booking settings live under `/venues/:id/booking-settings`.

exec: // Venue slugs are globally unique: generate a fresh one per run.

header.description: Resolves tenant context (looked up in the DB; an unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Tenant context required").

request.description:
**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active tenant-wide OWNER or STAFF of the tenant in `X-Tenant-Id` (`assertCanCreateVenue`). Venue-scoped staff cannot.

**Success:** 201 with a Venue `{ id, tenantId, name, slug, status, address, city, state, zipCode, country, timezone, phone, email, website, logo, coverImage, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`. New venues are PENDING. Saves `venueId` and `venueSlug`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown tenant context, missing `name`/`slug`, an invalid IANA `timezone`, or an invalid slug (3-63 chars, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing or double hyphen, not reserved like `www`, `app`, `api`, `admin`, `dev`, `test`, `demo`...).
- 403 when the caller cannot create venues in that tenant (including an owner sending another tenant's id).
- 409 when the slug is already taken by any venue.

**Notes:**
- The tenant comes from `X-Tenant-Id`, never the body. The pre-request script generates a unique slug. The booking-time script in Court booking assumes `timezone` stays Asia/Manila.

{
  "name": "Dev Club Downtown",
  "slug": "{{venueSlug}}",
  "address": "123 Rally St",

  "country": "PH",
  "timezone": "Asia/Manila",
  "phone": "+639171234567",
  "email": "venue@example.com",
  "description": "Local test venue created from Postman."
}

request.description:
**Who may call:** Any signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 `{ venues: Venue[] }`, every venue across all tenants, newest first.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 `{ id, tenantId, slug, name, status }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 when no venue has that slug.

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 with a Venue `{ id, tenantId, name, slug, status, address, city, state, zipCode, country, timezone, phone, email, website, logo, coverImage, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 when no venue has that id.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active OWNER/STAFF member of the venue's tenant whose membership is tenant-wide (no venue) or scoped to this venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanManageVenue`).

**Success:** 200 with the updated a Venue `{ id, tenantId, name, slug, status, address, city, state, zipCode, country, timezone, phone, email, website, logo, coverImage, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown venue (checked before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else, including staff scoped to a sibling venue.
- 400 for an invalid slug, `status`, or timezone.
- 409 when a new slug is already taken.

**Notes:**
- All fields optional; `status` is PENDING | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | INACTIVE. As sent it activates the venue, which booking needs.

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user.

**Success:** 200 `{ venueId, timezone, isDefault, minDurationHours, maxDurationHours, horizonDays, startAlignment, weeklyHours: { monday: { opensAt, closesAt } | null, ... } }`. When nothing is saved, returns the defaults with `isDefault: true` (1-8 h, 60 days ahead, HOUR starts, open 06:00 to midnight every day) without saving them.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown venue.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active OWNER/STAFF member of the venue's tenant whose membership is tenant-wide (no venue) or scoped to this venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanManageVenue`).

**Success:** 200 `{ venueId, timezone, isDefault, minDurationHours, maxDurationHours, horizonDays, startAlignment, weeklyHours: { monday: { opensAt, closesAt } | null, ... } }` with `isDefault: false`. Full replace (all fields required).

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown venue (before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else.
- 400 when a field is missing or out of range (durations 1-24 h, `horizonDays` 1-365, `startAlignment` HOUR | HALF_HOUR, times `HH:00` or `HH:30`), when `maxDurationHours` < `minDurationHours`, a day's hours are shorter than `minDurationHours`, or an overnight day runs past the next day's opening.

**Notes:**
- Each weekday is `{ opensAt, closesAt }` or `null` (closed). All seven keys must be present. `closesAt` at or before `opensAt` means the window runs past midnight (`00:00` = midnight).
- Court booking > Create booking books 18:00-20:00, inside these hours.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active OWNER/STAFF member of the venue's tenant whose membership is tenant-wide (no venue) or scoped to this venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanManageVenue`).

**Success:** 204 No Content; saved settings are removed and the venue falls back to the defaults. Idempotent.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown venue (before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active OWNER/STAFF member of the venue's tenant whose membership is tenant-wide (no venue) or scoped to this venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanManageVenue`).

**Success:** 204 No Content. Courts and booking settings are deleted with it.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown venue (before permissions).
- 403 for anyone else.
- 409 "Cannot delete venue with active bookings..." when any of its courts has bookings (booking history is never deleted).

**Notes:**
- Destructive: run last. Once you have booked, this returns 409.

item.description: Not versioned: `/courts/...`. List and create read the venue from `X-Venue-Id`.

**Who may call:** Platform admin, or an active OWNER/STAFF member of the venue's tenant whose membership is tenant-wide (no venue) or scoped to this venue (`AuthorizationService.assertCanManageVenue`).

**Success:** 201 with a Court `{ id, venueId, name, status, createdAt, updatedAt }`. New courts are ACTIVE. Saves `courtId`.

**Common refusals:**

- 400 for missing/unknown venue context or a missing `name`.
- 403 for anyone who cannot manage that venue.

**Notes:**
- The venue comes from `X-Venue-Id`, never the body.

**Success:** 204 No Content.

**Common refusals:**

item.name: Court booking
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/booking/...`. The venue comes from `X-Venue-Id`; the booker is always the signed-in user.

exec: // Builds a slot-aligned start 3 days ahead at 18:00 venue-local time.
// Assumes the venue timezone is Asia/Manila (UTC+08:00, no DST), as set by
// "Venues > Create venue". 3 days keeps Leave seat / Cancel outside the 24 h
// Open Play cutoff. Override by setting bookingStart yourself and
const day = new Date(Date.UTC(local.getUTCFullYear(), local.getUTCMonth(), local.getUTCDate() + DAYS_AHEAD));

header.description: Resolves venue (and its tenant) context. An unknown id is ignored and the route answers 400 "Venue context required".

request.description:
**Who may call:** Any signed-in user (no membership needed). The booking is owned by the caller; a spoofed email in the body is ignored.

**Success:** 201 `{ statusCode: 201, message, bookingReferenceID, bookingId?, openPlayJoinToken? }`. `bookingId` and `openPlayJoinToken` are only returned for Open Play bookings. Saves `bookingReferenceId`, `bookingId`, `openPlayJoinToken`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 for missing/unknown venue context; a `date` that is not a complete ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`Z` or `+HH:MM`, e.g. `2026-11-10T18:00:00+08:00`; date-only or offset-less input is rejected); `rentDuration` outside 1-24; `openPlayCapacity` outside 1-64; Open Play options on a private booking; or a venue rule violation: start in the past, beyond `horizonDays`, duration outside the venue's min/max, not on a slot boundary, or outside opening hours (evaluated in the venue's timezone).
- 404 when `courtId` is not a court of the `X-Venue-Id` venue.
- 409 "This court isn't taking bookings right now." unless court, venue and tenant are all ACTIVE; 409 when the slot overlaps an existing booking; 409 "Lots of players are booking..." when the court lock is busy.

**Notes:**
- The pre-request script sets `bookingStart` to 18:00 Asia/Manila three days from now (inside the PUT booking-settings hours, outside the 24 h Open Play cutoff). Sending twice gives 409 for the same slot; change `START_HOUR` or `DAYS_AHEAD` in the script.
- As sent this is a public Open Play game for 4 (the booker takes the first seat). For a private booking send `"isOpenPlay": false` and drop `openPlayCapacity` / `isOpenPlayPublic`.
- A private booking's id is not in the response. To try Open Play > Enable Open Play, look up the CourtBooking row by `referenceId` = `{{bookingReferenceId}}` (e.g. with Prisma Studio) and put its id in `privateBookingId`.

item.name: Open play
item.description: URI-versioned: `/v1/open-play/...`. The booking's venue/tenant always come from the booking itself; no X-Tenant-Id / X-Venue-Id is needed. "Venue staff" below means an active OWNER/STAFF membership in the booking's tenant that is tenant-wide or scoped to the booking's venue; unlike most routes, platform admin alone does NOT count.

query.description: Optional UUID: only games at this venue.
Optional ISO 8601 instant: games starting at or after this.
Optional ISO 8601 instant: upper bound on start time.

request.description:
**Who may call:** Public (`@AllowAnonymous()`), no session needed.

**Success:** 200 `{ items: [{ id, startsAt, venue: { id, name, slug, city, timezone }, court: { id, name }, capacity, confirmedSeats, isFull }], page, pageSize, total }`. Only future, active, publicly listed games.

**Common refusals:**
- 400 for a non-UUID `venueId`, a non-ISO `from`/`to`, or `page`/`pageSize` out of range.
- 429 when the rate limit is hit (default 100 requests / 60 s per client, then a 60 s block).

**Who may call:** Public or signed in (`@OptionalAuth()`); works for listed and unlisted games.

**Success:** 200 `{ listing, isPublic, viewer }`; `viewer` is `{ hasSeat, isBooker }` when signed in, `null` when signed out.

**Common refusals:**
- 404 for an unknown token, or a game that is not viewable (cancelled, venue not ACTIVE, booker deleted).

**Who may call:** The booker, or venue staff.

**Success:** 200 `{ listing, isPublic, isActive, joinToken, roster: [{ name, isBooker, joinedAt }] }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`).
- 404 when the booking does not exist or is not Open Play.
- 403 "Only the booker or staff of this venue can change this game." for anyone else.

**Who may call:** The booker, or venue staff.

**Success:** 200 `{ listing, isPublic, isActive, joinToken, roster: [{ name, isBooker, joinedAt }] }` with the new `isPublic`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`). Also 400 when `isPublic` is missing or not a boolean.
- 404 for an unknown booking.
- 403 for anyone else.
- 409 when the booking is not Open Play, is cancelled, or changed concurrently.

item.name: Enable Open Play on a private booking

request.description:
**Who may call:** Venue staff only (OWNER/STAFF membership; platform admin alone gets 403, see Tenant members > Add member).

**Success:** 200 `{ listing, isPublic, isActive, joinToken, roster: [{ name, isBooker, joinedAt }] }`; the booker takes the first seat and a join token is generated.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`). Also 400 for `capacity` outside 1-64 or a non-boolean `isPublic`.
- 404 for an unknown booking.
- 403 "Only staff of this venue can turn an existing booking into open play." for non-staff (the booker included).
- 409 when it is already Open Play, cancelled, already started, has no account holder, or changed concurrently.

**Notes:**
- Needs `privateBookingId`: a private booking's id is not returned by Create booking. Make a private booking, then find its id in the CourtBooking table by `referenceId` (see Court booking > Create booking).
- Both fields optional: `capacity` defaults to 4, `isPublic` to false.

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user (sign in as the second user first; the booker already has a seat).

**Success:** 201 `{ bookingId, confirmedSeats, capacity, isFull }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`).
- 404 when the game is unknown, not viewable, or not publicly listed (all give the same 404).
- 409 when the game has started, is full, you already have a seat, or the game changed / is busy.

**Notes:**
- Use either this or Join via link, not both: the second join by the same user is 409 "You already have a seat in this game."

**Who may call:** Any signed-in user; works for listed and unlisted games.

**Success:** 201 `{ bookingId, confirmedSeats, capacity, isFull }`.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 404 for an unknown token or a non-viewable (e.g. cancelled) game.
- 409 when started, full, already seated, or busy.

**Who may call:** A signed-in player who holds a (non-booker) seat.

**Success:** 204 No Content.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`).
- 404 when the booking is not Open Play, or you have no seat.
- 409 when the game is cancelled, you are the booker ("Cancel the booking instead"), it starts within 24 h, or it changed concurrently.

**Who may call:** The booker only (sign in as the owner again).

**Success:** 204 No Content; the booking is cancelled for everyone.

**Common refusals:**
- 401 when not signed in (no session cookie).
- 400 when `bookingId` is not a UUID (`ParseUUIDPipe`).
- 404 when the booking is not Open Play.
- 403 "Only the player who booked this court can cancel it." for anyone else, venue staff included.
- 409 when already cancelled, already started, other players hold seats and it starts within 24 h, or it changed concurrently.
